data.title: Analyzing STRK’s 15% fall, $2M in long liquidations — What’s next?
data.description:
While the wider market signaled a recovery from the recent sell-offs, Starknet wasn’t so lucky as it struggled under massive bearish pressure. In fact, since facing rejection at $0.12, the altcoin has closed at lower lows on the charts. 

Previously, the altcoin rallied amid speculation as investors turned bullish on its L1 plans for 2027. However, that speculation has since faded.

Over the last 24 hours, for example, STRK breached the $0.07-support, hitting a low of $0.069. At the time of writing, Starknet was trading at around $0.0707, down 15% on the daily charts.

The price drop was accompanied by a 60% decline in volume, indicating a sharp market slowdown as investors stayed away. 

Starknet long liquidations add to selling pressure

This extended decline on Starknet’s charts has seen bulls flushed out, with over $2 million in long positions liquidated.

The long liquidations increased selling pressure, further weakening the market. With liquidation risk remaining high, traders have significantly reduced their exposure too.

In fact, according to CoinGlass, over the last 24 hours, the altcoin has recorded $249 million in Futures outflows.

The selling pressure was even more intense over shorter timeframes. Over eight hours, Futures Netflow dropped to -$3.22 million as $41.98 million flowed out of the Futures market.

Typically, when sellers dominate the derivatives market, selling pressure can increase, resulting in further losses.

Protocol outflows exceed $59 million

In addition to sustained market exits, significant capital has flowed out of the protocol too. 

On 16th October, Protocol USD Inflows fell into negative territory, hitting -$59 million. A negative value alluded to higher outflows as users withdrew funds.

Often, higher protocol outflows could mean a fall in user participation and, in many cases, greater selling pressure too. 

What’s next for STRK?

As it stands, STRK is under pressure from two sides. Derivatives traders have lost confidence in the market, while the protocol is also seeing capital outflows.

As a result, southbound momentum has strengthened significantly. A look at the Relative Strength Index (RSI) seemed to support this bearish outlook too. Since forming a bearish crossover three days ago, the RSI has remained on a downward trajectory, falling to 53.

A falling RSI is indicative of weakening momentum. A drop below 50 would provide further evidence of increasing bearish pressure.

Therefore, if the current selling pressure continues, Starknet is likely to drop to $0.062, with October rally’s starting point at $0.055 acting as critical support.

However, a daily close above $0.075 would invalidate this bearish setup and open a path to reclaim $0.08 in the short term.

Final summary

  • Starknet [STRK] fell by 15%, breaching its $0.07 support, to a low of $0.069. 
  • Starknet saw $2 million in long liquidations, while protocol outflows rose to -$59 million.

data.title: Jupiter tests $0.29 demand zone as Solana DEX token mirrors Bitcoin’s pullback
data.description:
Jupiter’s [JUP] new trading product, YOLO, recorded over $1 billion in volume after its 15h October beta launch. Jupiter’s trading product on Solana offers 1,000x leverage on SOL, BTC, and ETH, and allows trading with as little as $10 to “make it big.”

Traders should remember that at that kind of leverage, a 0.1% price move against their direction could wipe out their position. As a simulated trading model, a single house pool funded by losers pays the winners, and the individual trades don’t make it to a real market, but of course the profits and losses are real.

Winners are paid when the platform’s liquidity pool can cover the entire amount, and there are no earlier claims in the queue.

The impact on JUP price trends

Jupiter’s long-term trend has been bullish since the swing structure break on the daily timeframe in May. The low made at $0.144 was the anchor point for the rally that pushed upwards to $0.388.

Since making this high earlier in October, Jupiter token’s price has declined by 21.8% so far.

The next long-term demand zone to watch will be at $0.22 (cyan), the bullish order block that propelled the latest JUP bullish impulse move.

Do bears have the upper hand?

On the 2-hour chart, the price trend shifted bearishly across the board. The demand zone at $0.32 was flipped to a supply zone too. The retest as resistance in recent days yielded a bearish reaction as well.

The next demand zone at $0.29 was already being tested at the time of writing. Given the wider market weakness due to Bitcoin’s [BTC] retracement towards $80K, it is likely that JUP would continue its descent over the next week.

A drop below $0.275 and a retest of $0.29 would likely offer short-term traders a selling opportunity.

Final Summary

  • The 1,000x Jupiter trading product on Solana recorded over $1 billion in trading volume after its 15th October beta launch.
  • Over the past ten days, JUP’s price has retraced by 21.8% and could slide further next week.

data.title: Why Venice Token’s AI expansion could push VVV price toward $30
data.description:
Venice Token [VVV] continues to advance after a successful bounce off from the $21 support zone, which was previously the resistance level that acted as a barrier against bears. At the time of writing, VVV surged by 10% in  the past 24 hours.

The rise follows the addition of new products with AI technology, namely Hy4 Preview, Muse Spark, and Muse Wonder by Venice. At the same time, VVV’s revenue growth has been aided by increased adoption of its AI solutions, with October generating the most revenue on the platform.

Could solid fundamentals aid VVV in breaking into the $30 liquidity cluster? 

Can VVV defend the $21 support?

VVV’s rebound follows repeated tests of the $21 price zone, which has shifted from resistance into a key support zone for the network bulls.

Remaining above this level will enable the bullish formation to be maintained and also provide the bulls a chance to attack stronger resistance. On the other hand, breaking down below the $21 level will undermine the bullish technical setup.

But with the token still trading above the 50-day, 100-day, and 200-day MAs, VVV’s long-term structure still leans on the favor of bulls. 

Is $30 VVV’s next target?

The next major barrier for the bulls sits around the $30 resistance level. The price level hosts an unmitigated liquidity cluster worth $31 million that could attract market attention, according to the liquidation heat maps data. 

If VVV manages to hold the support and buying activity gains momentum, then it could help the coin move towards this area. Revenue growth and AI product development will likely provide support to sentiment, but traders require further confirmation from the price action itself.

Currently, the focus should be on $21 as breaking below it might complicate the journey towards $30.

Final Summary

  • VVV rebounded from the $21 support zone after repeated tests, with buyers eyeing resistance near $30.
  • Venice Token’s expanding product lineup and reported revenue growth could strengthen sentiment, while a sustained break below $21 would weaken the bullish setup.

data.title: Celestia crypto hits 11-month high – Is $0.80 TIA’s next target?
data.description:
As the broader crypto market recovered, Celestia [TIA] bounced back from a $0.52 slip and reached an 11-month high of $0.71. 

However, at press time, Celestia was trading around $0.68, up 28% on the daily charts. Over the same window, the altcoin’s trading volume surged 160% to $162 million, indicating higher market participation. 

Additionally, the daily turnover rose from $32 million to $63 million, suggesting a higher buying pressure. 

Celestia rallies as bears face liquidation

After Celestia pumped, traders who had positioned themselves anticipating further price slip were flushed out of the market. 

According to CoinGlass data, the altcoin saw $1.4 million worth of shorts liquidated. Usually, when shorts are liquidated, it creates new buying pressure, pushing the price higher and triggering more short liquidations. 

In addition to buying pressure arising from short exits, more funds were allocated to open new positions. Notably, the altcoin’s Open Interest (OI) surged 45% to $142 million as of writing. 

The OI surge was backed by a 110% jump in volume, reflecting high participation and capital inflows. 

Investors on Binance increased capital deployment significantly. Over the past 24 hours, the Perps Buy Volume rose to 90 million compared to 89 million in Sell Volume. 

A higher buy volume indicated that more buy orders were executed during the period. 

Could profit takers threaten the rally?

While the pressure on the derivatives side turned to the upside, sellers on the spot became aggressive.  For example, on the 16th of October, Celestia’s Spot Netlow climbed to a record high of $2.2 million. 

Such an elevated Netflow implied that more tokens were deposited into exchanges than withdrawn.  Historically, higher exchange inflows have increased selling pressure, weakening market structure. 

Can the momentum hold?

Celestia’s upside momentum has strengthened significantly despite the recent profit realization. 

A look at the momentum indicators confirms this view. For instance, at the time of writing, the altcoin’s positive index of ADX rose to 31 while the negative index fell to 7. 

Rising +DI while the -DI declines indicated a strong upward momentum. Likewise, the Aroon line also validates this, with Aroon Up climbing to 100%. 

These indicators reflect sustained bullish pressure and signal a likely continuation of the trend. Thus, if these factors remain constant, Celestia will reclaim $0.70 and target $0.80, where the trend collapsed in November. 

However, if bulls fail to hold off profit-takers, the altcoin could retest $0.50.

Final summary

  • Celestia surged 28%, cleared key resistance, and reached an 11-month high of $0.71 before slightly retracing to $0.68.
  • TIA rallied, driven by strong speculative demand, but profit-taking could threaten these gains.

data.title: Up 11% after Coinbase, Deribit listing, can PONS breach $0.34 next?
data.description:
At press time, Pons [PONS] was up more than 11% in the last 24 hours after wiping out this week’s losses. In fact, it is now among the top trending tokens on the launchpad.

Pons and Cash Cat [CASHCAT] are the only tokens on Robinhood Chain that have a market cap of more than $100 million. The two rebounded after debuting on both Coinbase and Deribit exchanges.

PONS perps listed on Coinbase and Deribit

Both Coinbase and Deribit listed PONS perps on their markets in select jurisdictions, leading to high speculative trading. The tokens were offered at a 25x leverage.

For instance, Coinbase’s PONS/USD spot book did 5.1 million tokens in a few hours, which is roughly $1.80 million. All 30 PONS pools on Robinhood Chain did $27 million in volume.

Right now, V2 Graduated Pools hold 50.5% of the volume share, while V1 and V2 Bonding Curves hold 25.9% and 23.6%, respectively.

Additionally, the Open Interest (OI) of the token on Hyperliquid [HYPE] grew from $29.6 million to $33 million. This indicated that bulls were stacking the coin as the price was rising alongside the OI.

On the other hand, the OI of CASHCAT on the same exchange was $23.50 million.

However, the main catalyst remains support from Robinhood Chain, with CEO Vlad Tenev telling builders,

You matter to us.

The evidence is clear: The chain retained 94% of the spot flow, even though the listing was the main event. Such support could help the launchpad token recover. Especially as buybacks have dropped by 90%.

Here, it’s worth noting that the platforms are giving early investors more distribution. These buyers put in $27.6 million, but they now hold just $1.66 million.

PONS attempts falling wedge breakout

On the 4-hour chart, the altcoin was still 64% below its all-time high (ATH) at press time. Its price was attempting to break through the upper resistance of the massive month-long falling wedge pattern at $0.3454.

The bullish resurgence was also evidenced by the Bull Bear Power turning green, despite the weak momentum. The RSI at 53.96 also broke above the neutral level, reinforcing the return of market buyers.

Therefore, breaking above the resistance would confirm the start of a recovery. Conversely, if the level is not breached, the crypto will face significant bearish pressure as price movements contract. Usually, contraction precedes expansion.

Final Summary

  • PONS rallied by more than 11% amid its listing on Coinbase and Deribit, sparking speculative trading. 
  • PONS was nearing a falling wedge pattern breakout as bulls slowly returned despite early investors exiting.

data.title: ‘Perfect time for crypto’ — Why Arthur Hayes sees Bitcoin benefiting from AI bubble burst
data.description:
Arthur Hayes, CIO of crypto-focused Maelstrom Fund, believes the AI bubble will eventually burst, and it will be uber bullish for Bitcoin. 

In a recent interview with Luke Martin, Hayes said, 

AI is a waste of money. The bigger the AI bubble grows, the bigger the bailout will be, and the higher Bitcoin goes.

According to him, Anthropic, OpenAI, and SpaceX are all backed by the U.S government, but none of them makes money. Hayes foresees a “perfect time for crypto” if the AI bubble bursts. 

Put simply, the bailout will mean more government money printing, higher inflation, and investors fleeing to stores of value (SoV) such as gold and Bitcoin. This is popularly known as the debasement trade. 

Interestingly, BTC showed resilience this week and defended $80K despite a 2x-5x broader sell-off across AI/chipmakers and tech stocks. 

AI bubble: Bitcoin upside meets quantum risk

Delphi Research and Fidelity echoed a similar bullish outlook. For his part, Ceteris Paribus, the pseudonymous Head of Research at Delphi, noted, 

Getting quite bullish internet monies. Debasement from current debt situation + AI Ponzi bailout equal BTC flows.

An AI bailout will likely add to U.S fiscal debt and growing investors’ concerns. For perspective, U.S fiscal debt currently stands at $40.3T and is growing regardless of which party is in office. 

This has since triggered rising bond yields. According to Fidelity, this could worsen the U.S debt situation and further make the case for BTC.

The asset manager also said that the correlation between BTC and 10-year bond yields hit a record high of 0.6 in 2026. The yields rose by 10% in the past two months, and BTC surged by +30% over the same period. 

In other words, rising bond yields will likely send BTC higher if the correlation extends. 

If current debt and rate trends persist, it may not be long before the interest expense becomes the largest line item in the federal budget, further elevating focus on alternative stores of value

Still, Bitcoin’s quantum threat is intensifying with AI advancement and Google’s breakthroughs in quantum computers. For Ceteris, this could cap the expected BTC upside from the debasement trade. 

I think BTC will do quite well, but it won’t be the only SoV in the arena like it was a few years ago. Debasement bullish, but quantum will keep a cap on upside.

In the meantime, U.S Spot BTC ETFs bled another $228M this week, marking the second week of outflows in October. Still, this week’s capitulation showed cooling profits that may mark another bottom at $80K, as per Glassnode. 

Final Summary

  • AI bubble burst, and a likely bailout could trigger a debasement trade-driven BTC rally. 
  • Delphi Research cautioned that BTC’s upside could be capped by quantum risk.

data.title: Deutsche Bank, Charles Schwab double down on crypto as Bitcoin gains on TradFi
data.description:
From both short- and long-term perspectives, these two headlines could not have come at a better time.

First, Germany’s largest bank, Deutsche Bank, is preparing to launch crypto custody services. According to Reuters, the bank is just a few weeks away from launching the service in Germany. It will initially support Bitcoin and Ethereum, before moving on to stablecoins and eventually Asian markets in 2027.

That’s not all though as $13 trillion financial giant Charles Schwab has also officially launched Bitcoin and Ethereum trading for eligible clients. In this particular case, about 40 million accounts will be able to access BTC and ETH on the same platform where they trade stocks and bonds.

Collectively, these developments further reinforce the ongoing convergence of TradFi and DeFi, which is ultimately a signal that crypto is on the verge of becoming a mainstream investment category.

On a technical level, however, the institutional adoption comes at a time when Bitcoin is having difficulty holding above the psychologically important $80K-level. Meanwhile, Spot Bitcoin ETFs turned negative on the day as BlackRock alone reported four days of net outflows in the span of just one week, adding pressure to an already uncertain market setup.

Against this background, these developments could help Bitcoin hold key psychological levels in the short term. However, the bigger question is what Deutsche Bank and Charles Schwab have planned next for their crypto push.

According to AMBCrypto, their long-term digital asset strategies could define Bitcoin’s [BTC] institutional momentum in Q4.

Bitcoin vs. TradFi – Is institutional adoption reshaping the market cycle?

Two major TradFi players expanding their crypto services at the same time is hard to overlook.

According to AMBCrypto, the timing is particularly interesting. Despite the recent risk-off sentiment, Bitcoin closed out Q3 strongly on the back of institutional demand. Spot BTC ETFs saw over $6 billion in net inflows, marking the best quarterly performance of the year thus far. In this context, Charles Schwab opening BTC trading to 40 million accounts could further boost institutional and retail access to crypto.

The chart below highlighted another key trend. Despite macro FUD and rate hikes by the Federal Reserve, Bitcoin climbed by over 40% in Q3, compared to only 0.8% of the Nasdaq. This meant that BTC delivered a much better performance than the stock market, making it even more attractive to institutional investors.

In essence, heavyweights are looking to benefit from BTC’s growing outperformance over TradFi markets.

This trend will become more relevant as macroeconomic uncertainty rises in the near term. With U.S mid-term elections approaching, AI boom, and inflation pressures, the performance of BTC against the traditional market indexes can widen even more.

With this in mind, Deutsche Bank and Charles Schwab’s crypto expansion will boost institutional access to BTC. This could contribute to Bitcoin’s Q4 outlook as its outperformance to TradFi continues to gain attention.

Final Summary

data.title: CME Futures launch news fails to spur UNI’s price rally — What happened?
data.description:
On 22nd September, the world’s leading derivatives market, Chicago Mercantile Exchange (CME) Group, announced the launch of Bitcoin Cash [BCH] and Uniswap [UNI] Futures on 19th October.

In the last 24 hours, UNI’s price has declined by 1.24%, a performance on par with Bitcoin’s [BTC] 1.26% fall. The mood across the altcoin sphere appeared to be deflated in the short term.

No bullish impetus as Futures listing date nears

Over the past week, the governance token has oscillated between $6.80 and $7.80, establishing a short-term range.

The Futures Taker CVD (90-day) metric calculates the cumulative volume difference between market buy and sell orders over three months. It has been taker-sell dominated since 22nd September, with a decrease in volume too.

These appeared to be clear signs of aggressive sellers in control of the derivatives market for Uniswap. It could trigger a deeper price reset towards $5.

The 1-day price chart revealed a strongly bullish swing structure in place. It stretched from $3.17 in August to $$10.94, made in September. Since then, the altcoin has been in a retracement phase.

The retracement could extend deeper though. The Fibonacci retracement levels (yellow) underlined the $6.14 and $4.83 levels as the next potential targets in case of a sustained correction.

Traders’ call to action – Watch the short-term channel

AMBCrypto previously reported that Uniswap v4 processed $44 billion in 30-day trading volume. Alongside the protocol activity recovery, the $6.80 local support zone has been defended well so far.

The descending channel pattern (white) of the past ten days was still in play at press time. In fact, in recent hours, the price tested the mid-channel support and reacted positively.

Over the weekend, the $6.65-$6.70 area would be an important short-term demand zone. Swing traders can wait for Uniswap’s price reaction from this area to assess their next move.

Final Summary

  • Uniswap Futures Taker CVD has been negative since 22nd September, when the CME Group’s Uniswap Futures launch for 19th October was announced.
  • Over the past ten days, the altcoin has been trading within a falling channel and could dip below $7 once again.

data.title: Stablecoin supply has stalled in 2026, but payments rose by 45% to $480B: Report
data.description:
Stablecoin market supply eased in 2026 amid the broader crypto winter, but related payment volumes exploded by 45%. 

As of September, stablecoin payment volumes hit $482B, up from $331B seen last year during the same period. That marked a 45% surge on an annualized basis, primarily driven by businesses. 

According to the report, stablecoin payment volumes received by businesses increased by 37% from $179B to $246B. 

From a payment categories perspective, businesses dominated 64% of the volumes. 

Consumer-to-business transaction count nearly doubled as average payment size fell, while B2B value grew faster than count. Transfers between consumers gained share, but payments involving businesses still accounted for 64% of dollars moved.

When zoomed down to a quarterly basis, Q3 saw a record $72B in stablecoin payment volumes, with card-based spending exploding by 10x.

In fact, AMBCrypto had previously reported how stablecoin card spending was becoming a key adoption driver. 

The Allium report also acknowledged how crucial cards are in stablecoin adoption, especially for micro payments (spending of small amounts). 

Purchases under $50 accounted for 84% of the increase in visible card purchases, giving holders a way to spend small amounts without merchants adopting stablecoins.

Stablecoin supply remains flat above $300B

Despite the incredible growth in the payment verticals, however, the overall stablecoin supply closed September at around $304B. At the time of writing, the market cap stood at $302.9B, translating to less than 1% growth in 2026. 

The market is expected to hit $2T by 2028 and experts believe that stablecoin yield may be the missing catalyst to accelerate adoption. In fact, Ava Labs’ Olivia Vande Woude echoed a similar position, stating, 

$305B in stablecoins, and most of it earns nothing. The fix: fintechs plug into ready-made vaults that connect USDC, USDT, and EURC to diversified RWAs, with daily liquidity and on-chain transparency.

The ability to offer yield on stablecoin balances is limited by the GENIUS Act. In fact, EU regulators have banned stablecoin yield, even across DeFi platforms championed by Woude.

Interestingly, JPMorgan recently projected the sector could only grow to $500B-$600B by 2028 without the yield incentive. 

Overall, the stablecoin payment traction is impressive thanks to card spending and merchant payments. However, the broader adoption that can scale stablecoin supply may need more incentives, such as yield. 

Final Summary

  • Stablecoin payment volumes surged by 45% to over $480B in 2026.
  • Businesses dominated the payments volume thanks to stablecoin card usage, which exploded by 10x.

data.title: TIA crypto climbs nearly 17%—Can Celestia reclaim $0.70?
data.description:
Celestia’s TIA rose nearly 17% during the October 16 trading session, pushing beyond its recent price range. At the time of this writing, its price was around $0.69 after briefly reaching the $0.7233 price area.

The rally carried TIA above an area where it was not able to advance before now. Buyers now face the tests of recovering the $0.70 price area, and keeping the former trading ceiling beneath them if the price pulls back.

TIA clears its recent ceiling

The daily chart shows how far the recovery has gone. TIA traded near the $0.30 price area in August before it saw a series of stronger advances through September and October.

More recently, attempts to move beyond the $0.60–$0.63 price area struggled to hold. Friday’s surge cleared that area and took it to its highest level in the period shown.

Trading volume also saw a lot of increase, with around 51.47 million TIA exchanged at the time of this writing.

The larger volume bar shows that more trading accompanied the latest advance than during most recent sessions.

The market was still open, so its final gain and closing level were yet to be seen.

The retreat below $0.70 leaves work for buyers

The four-hour chart shows that the rally is slowing down after its initial burst. Smaller candles formed around the $0.70 price area, and this is followed by a small decline toward the $0.69 price area.

That pause does mean that the recovery has ended, but what it shows is that it has yet to hold comfortably above the round-number level.

If it is able to sustain a recovery above $0.70, the session high will be near the $0.723 price level. Buyers would need to overcome that high before another advance can be seen.

The daily Relative Strength Index [RSI] was near 70 at the time of this writing. This means we could see a rally, and it also signals caution. 

Where a pullback would test the recovery

Below the current price, the clearest area to watch is the $0.60–$0.63 price area.

If it’s able to hold there during a retreat, it would suggest that buyers are defending prices that previously led to some holders selling. But falling back below that area would weaken the latest breakout attempt.

If it sees a bigger price fall, the recent $0.53–$0.55 trading area will come back into view. But for now, the trend is improving with the closest obstacle at $0.70. Whether TIA retains its gains, or not, will give a better measure of the move’s strength.

Final Summary

  • TIA gained nearly 17% at the time of this writing, clearing recent highs.
  • Buyers need to recover the $0.70 price area, while the $0.60–$0.63 price level becomes an important area to defend during a pullback.
